title: Experimental Realization of a C-Shunt Flux-Qubit Coupler for Controlled-Z Gates between Transmons
authors: Weiping Yuan, Silu Zhao, Li Li, Chenglin Deng, Zhenghe Liu, Yu Liu, Tianming Li, Mingchuan Wang, Bingjie Chen, Guihan Liang, Jiacheng Song, Jinming Guo, Shuaili Wang, Mingxuan Zhou, Xiaohui Song, Kai Xu, Heng Fan, Zhongcheng Xiang, Dongning Zheng
abstract: Fast entangling gates and low-interaction idling require distinct operating conditions in superconducting quantum processors. We experimentally realize a transmon-C-shunt-transmon (TCT) device in which a flux-tunable, three-junction capacitively shunted flux-qubit coupler connects two transmon data qubits. The C-shunt coupler provides a flux-tunable, positively anharmonic spectrum for tailoring the interactions between the data qubits. Conditional Ramsey and swap measurements identify an idle region with near-zero residual ZZ interaction strength and suppressed transverse exchange. At this bias, simultaneous single-qubit interleaved randomized benchmarking yields X-gate fldelities above 99.7%, consistent with individual operation. A 45 ns nonadiabatic controlled-Z (CZ) gate achieves an interleaved randomized benchmarking fldelity estimate of 99.23(15)%. Numerical simulations identify coupler energy relaxation as an important limitation on CZ-gate fldelity and indicate that extending the coupler lifetime can improve gate performance. These results demonstrate the experimental feasibility of C-shunt flux-qubit couplers for combining low-interaction idling with fast entangling operations between transmon qubits.
summary: This paper reports the experimental realization of a C-shunt flux-qubit coupler connecting two transmon qubits. The device allows for precise tuning of qubit interactions, enabling the execution of a fast, high-fidelity Controlled-Z gate. The results confirm the feasibility of using such couplers to achieve both low-interaction idling and fast entangling operations.
main_problem: The challenge is to design a superconducting quantum processor that can perform fast, high-fidelity entangling gates while maintaining a low-interaction, low-error idling state.
main_result: The authors experimentally demonstrated a C-shunt flux-qubit coupler enabling a 45 ns Controlled-Z (CZ) gate with a fidelity of 99.23(15)%, while achieving single-qubit fidelities above 99.7%.
method: The work combines spectroscopic characterization, conditional Ramsey measurements to tune residual ZZ interactions, and randomized benchmarking to quantify gate fidelities.
model_or_system: The system is a transmon-C-shunt-transmon (TCT) device. The coupler is flux-tunable and provides a positively anharmonic spectrum, allowing precise control over the qubit-qubit interaction strength ($\zeta_{ZZ}$) and effective exchange ($g_{	ext{eff}}$).
key_observables: Single-qubit X-gate fidelities (>99.7%), CZ gate fidelity (99.23(15)%), residual ZZ interaction strength ($\zeta_{ZZ}$), and effective transverse exchange ($g_{	ext{eff}}$).
important_parameters: Gate time (45 ns), coupler anharmonicity ($\alpha_c/2\pi \simeq 703$ MHz), and energy relaxation times ($T_1$ for qubits and coupler).
main_assumptions: The primary limitation identified is coupler energy relaxation, which numerical simulations suggest can be mitigated by extending the coupler lifetime.
figures_summary: The figures likely present spectroscopy results mapping out the flux-tunable spectrum, Ramsey fringe patterns showing $\zeta_{ZZ}$ tuning, and benchmarking results quantifying gate fidelities.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of problem definition (need for tunable interaction), characterization (spectroscopy, measuring $\zeta_{ZZ}$ and $g_{	ext{eff}}$), gate implementation (CZ gate sequence), and performance benchmarking (RB measurements).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it demonstrates a concrete, hardware-level solution for controlling qubit interactions in superconducting circuits, a core topic in quantum information processing.
